summary: Configured persistent internal DNS on node1. node2 now uses node1 as its resolver, and inventory-api.internal resolves to node2 (10.100.219.11). Both nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities and working DNS.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled dnsmasq on node1.
Configured inventory-api.internal → 10.100.219.11 with upstream DNS forwarding.
Permanently allowed DNS through node1's firewall.
Configured node2's NetworkManager connection to use 10.100.219.10 exclusively for DNS.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified persistence.

evidence.requirement: node1 runs the internal DNS resolver and returns node2 for inventory-api.internal
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is active/enabled, listens on 10.100.219.10:53, and directly answers 10.100.219.11.

evidence.requirement: node2 uses node1 for DNS and resolves internal lookups
evidence.summary: NetworkManager persistently specifies 10.100.219.10, resolv.conf uses it, and the internal name resolves correctly.
Boot ID changed from 67c52137-ce51-4fec-b441-23966cea63a8 to ec363a73-8248-4730-abc7-e75ce5cdf743; DNS service, firewall access, record data, and downstream resolution recovered.
